AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: The literature shows that the performance of densely sintered zirconia single crowns seems to be unaffected by the cement material. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effects of various cement materials on the stress distribution in a monolithic translucent zirconia crown.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A crown-cement-dentin complex was modeled. Six cements were evaluated: zinc phosphate, glass-ionomer, resin-modified glass-ionomer, dual-cure resin, calcium aluminate-based, and a theoretical or conceptual cement with mechanical properties close to those of dentin (ie, monoblock cement).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: While varying stress concentrations were found within the cements, the stress concentrations in the crown and dentin were consistent irrespective of cement material.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Within the limitations of this study, it can be concluded that cement material had a negligible effect on stress distribution in the monolithic zirconia crown.

Article.ArticleTitle: Limited Effect of Cement Material on Stress Distribution of a Monolithic Translucent Zirconia Crown: A Three-Dimensional Finite Element Analysis.
